summary.text: Alan Bond, an independent with degrees from Dartmouth College and Harvard Business School who has worked in business strategy, lost the November 3, 2026 election for New Jersey's 11th Congressional District to Analilia Mejia.
He ran on the Hope for Tomorrow Party line and had received 0.5% of the vote in the April 2026 special election for this seat.

In a statement published by the New Jersey Globe, he said he ran because many residents feel the two-party system does not fully represent them, and listed affordability, infrastructure, and protecting Social Security as priorities.

paragraphs.text: Alan Bond earned a bachelor's degree from Dartmouth College and a graduate degree from Harvard Business School, and Ballotpedia lists his career experience as working in business strategy.

He ran as an independent in the April 16, 2026 special election for NJ-11 and received 625 votes, or 0.5%. He was not invited to an April 1, 2026 debate between Mejia and Hathaway, and the New Jersey Globe published his written response.
He was on the November 3, 2026 ballot on the Hope for Tomorrow Party line.
He received 0.9% of the vote to Analilia Mejia's 60.8%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
